_note: GENERATED by `go run ./scripts/evalindex`. The cards are authored; their claims about coverage are checked against the repository by the companion test, because a registry free to say whatever it likes about how well kapi is measured would be the opposite of evidence.

questions.ask: Does content survive being read and written back?
questions.why: Everything else is downstream of this. A format kapi reads imperfectly is a format whose translations land in a document that no longer matches the original.

questions.ask: Is approved wording reused when the rules still hold, and refused when they do not?
questions.why: The reason to keep a content memory at all. Reusing too little wastes reviewed work; reusing too much writes wording that was approved under rules that have since moved.

questions.ask: Does the governance actually reach the model, rather than only checking its output?
questions.why: A voice profile that is enforced only after generation is a correction loop. One that is in the prompt is a steer, and the difference shows up in how much there is to correct.

questions.ask: Do the checks find the violations they claim to find?
questions.why: A check that misses is worse than no check: it reports a clean run over content nobody has looked at.

questions.ask: Is source authoring governed the same way translation is?
questions.why: kapi governs content, not only translations. If the English is off-voice and off-terms, every language downstream inherits it, and nothing here measures whether kapi helps.

questions.ask: What does a run cost, and is that what we said it costs?
questions.why: A quality improvement that triples the token bill is a trade, not an improvement, and it should be visible as one.

questions.ask: Where does kapi stand against the alternatives?
questions.why: The question a reader has and we cannot answer from the inside. Measuring it needs independent ground truth, and publishing it means publishing the losses too.

evals.title: Filter parity against upstream Okapi
evals.corpus: The Okapi Framework's own filter test suite, mapped onto neokapi's readers.
evals.covers: Whether a document read by neokapi produces the same content model as the Java implementation it descends from, per format.
evals.misses: Publishes nothing. The report lands in a gitignored sandbox and the dashboard that used to render it was retired, so the result is visible only to whoever ran it. Formats with no upstream counterpart are unmeasurable this way, and a known-failure list is carried rather than fixed.

evals.title: Format maturity, L0 to L4
evals.corpus: Every registered format, scored against a fixed rubric.
evals.covers: How far each format has been taken: read, write, round-trip, inline codes, faithful write-back.
evals.misses: A rubric level is a claim about capability, not about quality on your documents.

evals.title: KBF conformance across engines
evals.corpus: The KBF conformance suite, run against the Go engine compiled to WebAssembly and the TypeScript mirror.
evals.covers: That two independent implementations of the bundle format agree, operation by operation, in your browser.
evals.misses: Runs only when someone opens the page. Nothing in CI executes it, so it reports rather than gates. The structural and envelope checks run on the Go engine alone.

evals.title: What an author's edit does to reuse
evals.corpus: One approved sentence pair, edited eleven ways; a three-sentence paragraph; five governance scenarios.
evals.covers: Which rules apply where, whether an edited source still gets its approved translation, whether a prior version is offered or withheld, and what reaches the prompt.
evals.misses: One language pair. The edit ladder is one sentence, chosen for length rather than sampled.

evals.title: Whether the prior version changes what the model writes
evals.corpus: Six wording cases with a control, plus a 20-block document in three batching arms.
evals.covers: Whether showing the model a block's previously approved translation keeps the approved wording, and what it costs in calls and tokens.
evals.misses: One model, one language pair, one direction. The judged half has no measured agreement with a person; only the deterministic consistency half should be relied on.
evals.settings: Not recorded, and not pinned. Anthropic's default sampling applies, so a re-run samples afresh.

evals.title: What context injection is worth
evals.corpus: A synthetic brand corpus with a fixed rubric, swept across models.
evals.covers: Whether a model given voice guidance and terminology produces output that needs less correction than one that is not.
evals.misses: Judge-to-human agreement is gated at 30 labelled items; the literature puts the useful floor at 100 to 200, and no sweep has cleared even the lower bar.
evals.settings: Not recorded, and not pinned. Each swept model runs at its own API default.

evals.title: What each call actually sends
evals.corpus: The prompts built for the reuse evals, captured as they went to the model.
evals.covers: That the voice guide, the terminology a call can use, and a block's prior version are in the prompt, and that the cache key moves with them.
evals.misses: Reads the prompt kapi built, not the reply it got. It shows the governance arrived; whether the model followed it is context-value's question.

evals.title: Precision and recall of the content checks
evals.misses: Three of the five checks are not measured at all: term-check, voice-check and voice-vocab-check. Ten cases is too few to separate a real precision difference from noise.

evals.title: Whether source checks find real violations
evals.corpus: Needs a labelled corpus of source content carrying known voice and terminology violations.
evals.covers: Would measure term-check, voice-check and voice-vocab-check the way check-accuracy measures the other two.
evals.misses: Not built. These three checks ship and nothing measures whether they are right.

evals.title: Whether governed authoring changes the output
evals.corpus: Needs source content and a voice profile with something to say about it.
evals.covers: Would be the authoring counterpart of reuse-effect: whether content written or rewritten under a voice profile differs, and differs in the direction the profile asks for.
evals.misses: Not built. kapi's authoring-side claim currently rests on no measurement.

evals.title: Whether an inferred voice profile is usable
evals.corpus: Needs corpora with hand-authored reference profiles to compare a draft against.
evals.covers: Would measure whether voice-infer's draft resembles what a person would have written from the same corpus.
evals.misses: Not built, and the hardest of the three: it needs reference profiles that do not exist yet.

evals.title: What batching costs and saves
evals.corpus: A fixed corpus swept across batch sizes and models.
evals.covers: Throughput and structural integrity as blocks per call rises, priced per model.
evals.misses: Concurrency is recorded because throughput depends on it, so two models swept at different concurrencies cannot be raced on speed.
evals.settings: Not recorded, and not pinned. Concurrency is recorded; the sampling settings are not.

evals.title: What a local model costs to run
evals.corpus: The bundled ML models, on one machine's runtime.
evals.covers: What a user pays in download size, cold start, per-sentence inference and resident memory.
evals.misses: Measured on one platform. A different runtime or accelerator moves every number.

evals.title: Engine throughput
evals.corpus: 844 fixtures on the pseudo-translation path, which exercises read and write without a model.
evals.covers: How fast the engine moves content when no provider is in the way, per format and per engine.
evals.misses: Isolates the engine deliberately, so it says nothing about a run that calls a model.

evals.title: kapi against other converters
evals.corpus: Needs a document corpus and independent ground truth, meaning rendered pages rather than another tool's output.
evals.covers: Would measure conversion speed and fidelity against markitdown, pandoc, docling, unstructured and LibreOffice.
evals.misses: Not built here. A harness of this shape exists in the anydoc repository and already includes kapi in its speed tables; neokapi publishes nothing of its own.
